title: Root-Finding Methods
description: Bisection, fixed-point iteration and Banach's theorem, Newton and secant methods, order of convergence.
html:
🎯 Root-Finding Methods

1. Bisection

Interval $[a,b]$ with $f(a)f(b) < 0$, midpoint $m = \frac{a+b}{2}$, keep the half with the sign change.

$$|x_k - x^*| \le \frac{b-a}{2^{k+1}}$$

Always convergent but only linear (factor $\tfrac12$). Example $x^3 - x - 2$ on $[1,2]$: $1.5,\ 1.75,\ 1.625,\ 1.5625,\ \ldots \to 1.5214$.

2. Fixed-Point Iteration & Banach

$$x_{k+1} = \varphi(x_k), \quad |\varphi'| \le L < 1 \text{ on } [a,b], \ \varphi([a,b]) \subseteq [a,b]$$

$$|x_k - x^*| \le \frac{L^k}{1-L}|x_1 - x_0| \;\;(\text{a priori}), \qquad |x_k - x^*| \le \frac{L}{1-L}|x_k - x_{k-1}| \;\;(\text{a posteriori})$$

Linear convergence with factor $|\varphi'(x^*)|$. The same equation has good and bad rearrangements.

3. Newton and Secant

$$x_{k+1} = x_k - \frac{f(x_k)}{f'(x_k)}, \qquad x_{k+1} = x_k - f(x_k)\frac{x_k - x_{k-1}}{f(x_k) - f(x_{k-1})}$$

Example $\sqrt2$

$x_0 = 2 \to 1.5 \to 1.416667 \to 1.414216 \to 1.414214$. Errors: $5.9\cdot10^{-1},\ 8.6\cdot10^{-2},\ 2.5\cdot10^{-3},\ 2.1\cdot10^{-6},\ 1.6\cdot10^{-12}$.

4. Order of Convergence

$$|e_{k+1}| \le C|e_k|^p, \qquad p \approx \frac{\ln(e_{k+1}/e_k)}{\ln(e_k/e_{k-1})}$$

  • Bisection, fixed point: $p = 1$. Newton (simple root): $p = 2$, for a multiple root $p = 1$. Secant: $p \approx 1.618$.
  • Modified Newton $x_{k+1} = x_k - m f/f'$ for an $m$-fold root.

5. Which Method? Typical Mistakes

  • Safety needed: bisection. Fast and $f'$ available: Newton (safeguard with bisection). Without $f'$: secant.
  • Newton fails for $f' \approx 0$, cycles, bad starting values, root singularities ($\sqrt[3]{x}$).
  • Stopping only on $|x_{k+1} - x_k|$ – better also check $|f(x_k)|$.
  • Starting bisection without a sign change.
